description.narrative:
Den förslagna insatsens syfte är att bidra till rättighetsbaserad samt ökad tillgång till sexuell och reproduktiv hälsa och rättigheter (SRHR) services i Etiopien. Detta syfte är högst relevanta i den etiopiska kontexten där det beräknas att över en tredjedel av tonåringar och ungdomar inte har tillgång till sådana tjänster.
Mer specifikt, insatsen syftar till att främja följande rättigheter: -Rätten att själva bestämma om, när och hur många barn man ska ha. -Rätten till SRHR-relaterad information och services. -Rätten att vara fri från könsrelaterat våld.
För att uppnå detta mål kommer unga kvinnors och mäns egenmakt att stärkas som ”rättighetsbärare” för kunna kräva sina SRHR medans service leverantörer och utbildare kommer att stärkas som ”ansvarstagare” för att skapa en möjliggörande miljö för unga människor att utöva sina rättigheter. Insatsens fokus är därför:
-Förbättra kvinnors och flickors förmåga till att utöva sina SRHR. -Förbättra ansvarsutkrävning avseende ansvarstagare och minska diskriminering av kvinnors och flickors tillgång till SRHR-information och service. -Stärka den möjliggörande miljön på interpersonell- och familjenivå för att stödja kvinnor och flickor att kräva och utöva SRHR.
Fokus kommer att omfatta uppföljning och utvärdering och lärande.
Totalt kommer insatsen att nå 7680 flickor och pojkar i Addis Ababa under tre år. Projektet kommer att piloteras i Addis Abeba, med målet att skapa en replikerbar modell för att expandera till andra områden efter piloten. Addis Abeba har valts ut som pilotplats främst på grund av de stora koncentrationerna av unga människor och den ökande migrationsgraden till staden från landsbygden.

The focus of the project is to: -Improve women and girls’ agency to exercise their SRHR in Ethiopia. -Improve duty bearers’ accountability and reduce discrimination towards women and girls’ access to SRH information and services. -Strengthen the enabling environment at interpersonal and family level to support women and girls to demand and exercise SRHR.
In order to achieve this goal, young women and men will be empowered as the “rights holders” to demand their SRHR while service providers and educators will be strengthened as the “duty bearers” to create an enabling environment for young people to exercise these rights.
Focus will also be on monitoring and evaluation and learning.
The project will reach 7,680 girls and boys over three years. The project will be piloted in Addis Ababa, with the aim to create a replicable model to expand into other areas after the pilot. Addis Ababa has been selected as the pilot location primarily for the large concentrations of young people and the increasing rates of migration into the city from rural areas.

The foundation for this program are the following rights based goals: (1) the right to decide, if, when, and how many children to have, (2) the right to sexual and reproductive health (SRH) information and services (3) the right to be free from violence.
These overarching goals are supported by the following objectives: • Improve womens and girls agency to exercise their SRHR. • Improve duty bearers accountability and reduce discrimination toward women and girls that hinders access to SRH information and services. • Strengthen the enabling environment at interpersonal and family levels to support women and girls to demand and exercise SRHR.

Over the program period, RBA has initiated SRHR education and awareness in Addis Ababa to improve AYSRH services. The program has trained educators, healthcare providers, law enforcement bodies and key decision makers to build their capacity and improve values/attitude towards SRH, GBV, and gender. The program has also supported the city administration GBV prevention and response efforts through strengthening a communitybased GBV prevention committee, initiating helpline for GBV, strengthening GBV services by establishing two onestop centres, and providing technical assistance for three existing sites.
Furthermore, the project facilitated action oriented awareness creation and advocacy events on gender equality and social inclusion, and meaningful youth participation. The program has since early 2022 also supported emergency GBV response integrated with mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS) and addressed SRHR needs of women and girls in conflict affected areas of Amhara and Afar. It has trained healthcare professionals on the minimum initial service package (MISP) for SRH in crisis, and GBV to improve availability of SRH services trained community volunteers to enhance GBV case identification, provide MHPSS first aid, and assist with referrals to onestop centres supported establishment/strengthening of 15 onestop centres for comprehensive, survivorcentred GBV response (for humanitarian response in Afar and Amhara) and supported SRHR service restoration at 65 catchment facilities through capacity building, provision of essential equipment, and regular supervision. The program teams have engaged in various relevant platforms at global, national, and regional level as an active member promoting accountability, respecting human rights, and fostering improved ownership by the responsible sectors. The teams worked with other members of the technical working group (TWG) to incorporate a gender, youth, and social inclusion (GYSI) lens in guidelines and policies and prioritize SRH and GBV in humanitarian response. For example, an updated code of conduct for GBV prevention in school settings, the national GBV policy (which is in the pipeline to be approved by the parliament), and regional GBV response strategy.
Some examples of results in numbers: -In Addis Ababa, the project supported 98 public health facilities efforts to improve the availability and accessibility of Adolescent and Youth Sexual and Reproductive Health (AYSRH) services focused on Comprehensive Contraceptives (CC), Comprehensive Abortion Care (CAC), and SGBV screening, and referral to nearby onestop centers. Further, the program has provided comprehensive support including strengthening the knowledge and skills of providers in these service areas. -The program has also trained over 2,723 SRH service providers (duty bearers), established a youth advisory council (YAC) comprised of 15 volunteer members, and educated 10,822 young people on SRHR. In addition to the technical skills, EngenderHealth has also integrated tools such as VCAT and GYSI to improve the soft skills needed to provide nondiscriminatory/ nonjudgmental AYSRH services. -A total of 3,809 survivors received a comprehensive lifesaving service at 18 onestop centers (three existing sites and 15 established through the projects effort, 2 in Addis Ababa, 11 in Amhara, and 2 in Afar). -Community referral contribution to onestop centers has rached 21%. -Through the partnership with Ethiopian Women Lawyers Association (EWLA), 1,864 GBV survivors received free legal service while a total of 963,993 women and girls were served with comprehensive contraception (CC) and 88,020 comprehensive abortion care (CAC) services.
Source: EngenderHealth´s Final Narrative Report (UM2019/31456/ADDI60)
